definitions.explanation: The buttocks or gluteal area of the body, treated as an anatomical region. This is the formal, technical term used in medical, anatomical, and fitness contexts, as opposed to everyday words like お{尻|しり}.

examples.japanese: {臀部|でんぶ}の{筋肉|きんにく}を{鍛|きた}える。
examples.english: To train the muscles of the buttocks.

examples.japanese: {注射|ちゅうしゃ}は{臀部|でんぶ}に{打|う}ちます。
examples.english: The injection is given in the buttocks.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}{座|すわ}っていると{臀部|でんぶ}に{痛|いた}みが{出|で}ることがある。
examples.english: Sitting for long periods can cause pain in the buttocks.

examples.japanese: このトレーニングは{臀部|でんぶ}と{太|ふと}もも{裏側|うらがわ}の{筋肉|きんにく}を{同時|どうじ}に{刺激|しげき}する{効果|こうか}があります。
examples.english: This exercise has the effect of stimulating the muscles of the buttocks and the back of the thighs at the same time.

notes:
Composed of {臀|でん} (buttocks — a kanji used almost exclusively in this compound and a few medical terms) and {部|ぶ} (part, region).

REGISTER:
{臀部|でんぶ} is a clinical, anatomical word. You will encounter it in medical documents, fitness and exercise articles, anatomy textbooks, and physical therapy contexts. In ordinary conversation, Japanese speakers say お{尻|しり} (or simply {尻|しり}) instead. Using {臀部|でんぶ} in casual speech would sound oddly formal or euphemistic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {臀部|でんぶ}の{筋肉|きんにく}: the gluteal muscles
- {臀部|でんぶ}{痛|つう}: pain in the buttocks
- {臀部|でんぶ}に{注射|ちゅうしゃ}する: to inject into the buttocks
- {臀部|でんぶ}{下垂|かすい}: sagging of the buttocks

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{尻|しり}: bottom, butt — the everyday, conversational word
- {尻|しり}: butt — blunter, sometimes vulgar without the お
- {大臀筋|だいでんきん}: gluteus maximus — the specific muscle name
- {腰|こし}: lower back, hip area — overlapping but distinct region
